rationale: Short turn refining the @joint_apply_order question after re-reading the joint/auto-leave path, because the first hypothesis as written ('an application that applies out of order, or a proposal the leader's stale check let through') is too loose to test. Under in-order application the panic should be unreachable: the leave-joint entry is proposed by appliedTo as soon as the joint change is applied at the leader, it occupies an index after the joint change, and any later joint-entering change is appended only after it, so a follower applying its own log in order is non-joint again by the time it reaches the new change. The leader-side check reinforces this: stepLeader rewrites a joint-entering change to a normal entry whenever the leader's own tracker is joint, so the entry can only be appended while the leader is non-joint. The open possibilities therefore narrow to two, and both are testable: either the harness applied changes out of the order its own log provided (a harness defect, which the reverted sweep cannot rule out but the panic's location in a skipped-apply model makes plausible), or a permitted history exists in which the leave entry never precedes the new joint change at some node - for instance a leader that never applied the joint change while leading so appliedTo never proposed the leave, a leadership change that leaves the leave-joint proposal unpursued, or a change whose entry the application is entitled to apply later than the new one because the two arrived in different terms. I updated the investigation's hypothesis and discriminator to that narrower form; no experiment is requested this turn because the deterministic prefix is not written yet.

investigations.hypothesis: Under an application that applies its own committed log in order, a joint-entering change should never be applied at a node whose tracker is still joint, because the leave-joint entry for the previous joint configuration precedes it in the log and is proposed by the leader's own appliedTo path as soon as that joint change is applied; the leader-side rewrite in stepLeader also keeps such a change out of the log while the leader's configuration is joint. The panic therefore indicates one of two things: the applying party did not apply in log order (harness defect), or a permitted history exists in which the leave-joint entry never precedes the new joint change at that node - a leader that never applied the joint change while leading, a leadership change after which no one pursues the leave, or entries from different terms that the application may see in an order the contract does not require.
investigations.discriminator: Deterministic prefix rather than random sweep: (i) reproduce the harness panic and print the entry (index, term, type) sequence the panicking node applied, which distinguishes out-of-order application from a missing leave; (ii) build the reachability variant - three voters, joint change with AutoLeave, isolate or step down the leader before it applies the joint change so no leave is proposed, then have a new leader append a joint-entering change, and observe what the previously lagging node applies and in what order; (iii) control where the same prefix keeps every application current, which should never panic. The discriminator is the first case that panics while the applied entry order matches the log order, with the entry types and terms of the two joint changes and the absence of a leave entry printed.
